summary.text:
Global equity markets retreated amid escalating geopolitical tensions following Iranian strikes on Kuwait, Bahrain, and US military sites during the ongoing Hormuz crisis. US indices closed firmly lower, with the Dow Jones down 1.64% and the S&P 500 falling 1.03%, driving the VIX up 11.13% to 25.46. European markets also slumped, led by a 2.15% drop in the Euro Stoxx 50.

In currency markets, the US dollar index edged up 0.17% to 103.668, with the euro falling 0.12% to 1.0985 and sterling up 0.06% to 1.3193. Commodities faced broad declines, with Brent crude falling 0.62% to 92.56, WTI slipping 1.48% to 84.74, and gold dropping 1.85% to 3792.8999.

Looking ahead, market participants are monitoring further developments in the Gulf conflict, as well as geopolitical shifts as Vladimir Putin promotes a Eurasian order ahead of a planned meeting with Xi Jinping and Donald Trump.
